themes.title: Anthropic's ~$1.5tn IPO moves ahead
themes.summary: Anthropic has filed its S-1 and will press ahead with an IPO targeting around a $1.5 trillion valuation, with the roadshow scheduled for next week. The listing lands against a sharp post-midterm tech selloff, making it the defining test of investor appetite for pure-play frontier AI in public markets.
themes.angle: The clearest signal yet that generative-AI value creation is shifting from private to public markets.

themes.title: GCC doubles down on AI and quantum capital
themes.summary: Regional AI investment is escalating across the GCC. Aramco is reported to invest $2.6 billion in the AI firm Humain, the UAE opened its first dedicated humanoid-robot showroom, Abu Dhabi's AIREV took strategic investment from Terra Invest, and an Abu Dhabi maritime academy partnered on quantum logistics.
themes.angle: GCC capital is flowing beyond conventional AI software into robots, quantum, and flagship national champions.

themes.title: AI backlash: data centers meet the electorate
themes.summary: Protests against data centers continued across Europe over the weekend, and political resistance to AI infrastructure is colliding with the capex buildout that underpins the AI trade. CoreWeave is courting the incoming Texas administration as markets price in a post-election reality check on AI spending.
themes.angle: Permitting and community politics, not just chip supply, are becoming the binding constraint on AI capacity.

themes.title: US midterms reset the AI policy table
themes.summary: Candidates favouring stricter AI oversight won key US congressional races after a $110 million advocacy push partly backed by Anthropic, while surveys show growing public anxiety about the AI boom. Commentators read this as a durable shift toward more AI legislation and a harder political environment for Big Tech capex.
themes.angle: The midterms turned AI from a tech story into an electoral and regulatory axis.

themes.title: Enterprise AI economics: Gartner's software forecast
themes.summary: Gartner projects global software spend reaching $1.68 trillion in 2027, up 14.6%, with the fastest-growing segments being foundation models (up ~117%) and AI application platforms (up ~39%). Enterprise AI budgets are becoming a structural growth line rather than an experiment.
themes.angle: Hard numbers that frame the enterprise-AI market for board conversations.

themes.title: GCC wealth-tech: investors want humans in the loop
themes.summary: A report from fintech platform Avloq finds GCC investors favour AI-assisted wealth advice over full automation, a differentiated sentiment versus Western markets pushing toward robo-advisory. Separately, DIFC courts proposed a framework for rulings involving tokenized assets and DIFC-based cross-border payment tech keeps expanding.
themes.angle: GCC clients trust AI as an assistant, not an autonomous decision-maker - a placement difference worth surfacing.

themes.title: Startup funding and AI M&A heats up
themes.summary: AI-native deal flow stays hot: image/video-gen startup Fal raised at a $16 billion valuation and CrowdStrike struck two acquisitions, while SoftBank and ABB weigh carving out the Chinese part of a robotics deal blocked in Beijing, and Meta's strategy chief Dave Wehner moves to Fireworks as CFO.
themes.angle: Funding, talent, and capacity are rotating aggressively around the agents/robotics/infra stack.
